--- title: "CTEDemographics" editor: visual --- # Data prep Now I'm going to prep the CTE demographics dataset to join with the master. I will first load the entire CTE demographics dataset, clean it up, and then join with my master/Central graduate dataset.
::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} | PersonID| FiscalYearTimeID|Grade |BasicParticipant |BasicConcentrator |BasicCompletor |Concentrator150 | |--------:|----------------:|:-----|:----------------|:-----------------|:--------------|:---------------| | 9143238| 20200630|10 |Y |N |N |N | | 277021| 20200630|12 |Y |N |N |Y | | 11651683| 20200630|10 |Y |N |N |N | | 10737120| 20200630|12 |Y |N |N |Y | | 8872775| 20200630|12 |Y |Y |Y |Y | | 4002413| 20210630|10 |Y |N |N |N | ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} |x | |:-----------------| |PersonID | |FiscalYearTimeID | |Grade | |BasicParticipant | |BasicConcentrator | |BasicCompletor | |Concentrator150 | ::: :::
The original dataset provides whether the student was a basic participant, basic concentrator, basic completor, and/or a centrentrator 150 when taking a CTE course. It looks like each observation is unique by grade of the student. This means that one PersonID can have multiple observations. In order to determine how I want to organize this data so that each observation represents the full characteristics of each PersonID I need to understand how these values are defined. - Basic Participant: Any grade 9-12 student who successfully completes one or more state-approved CTE course(s). - Basic Concentrator: this is the old standard for years and required the student complete 240 hours. Any student successfully enrolled in a single CTE field for more than 240 hours (successful is defined as passing grade). - Basic Completor: any concentrator who attains academic and technical knowledge and skills and graduates from high school. - Concentrator 150: This is the new standard - Any grade 9-12 student who successfully completes 150+ course hours (or more) as part of a state-approved secondary CTE program, within one career field. Judging by these definitions, it seems that we will want three categories; 1. Those that participated in a CTE course but were not a concentrator or a completor, and 2. Those that participated in a CTE course and graduated as a concentrator. 3. Those that did not participate in a CTE course. So essentially, filtering this dataset to provide the "highest level achieved" in terms of CTE coursework. We will focus on filtering this dataset to the highest level achieved and will then join with the graduate list which will have all the individuals that did not participate in any CTE courses.
::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} | PersonID|cte.achievement | |--------:|:-----------------------------| | 141|CTE Concentrator or Completor | | 198|CTE Participant | | 1004|CTE Concentrator or Completor | | 1103|CTE Concentrator or Completor | | 1104|CTE Concentrator or Completor | | 1180|CTE Concentrator or Completor | ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} |x | |:---------------| |PersonID | |cte.achievement | ::: :::
When joined with the master file, there were 96,410 that were either a CTE participant or concentrator. This is below the \~115,556,000 that took at least one CTE course according to the CTE enrollment dataset. This could mean that there roughly 20,000 students that took a CTE course but did not graduate. Lets join this dataset with the master to confirm this thought.

After joining with the master dataset, we have 137,622 rows and 47 columns.
# Summary of CTE demographics We will summarize the CTE demographics data by rural-ness and region to see if there's any significant differences. First, lets see what percentage of the graduates by cte demographics categories. The table below shows that of the total graduates from Central high schools, 40% were a CTE concentrator or completor, while 30% were just a participant and 30% took no CTE courses at all.
::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: :::
The cross-tabs show a significant difference between the percentage of students by categorization and RUCA categories. The largest difference is entirely urban schools where 34% of the graduates had no CTE.

The highest percentage of No CTE graduates is Sherburne County with 42.5% and Pine not far behind with 40%.
